title: Citizens' assemblies
script: Narrator: In a small town in Europe, forty ordinary residents were chosen by lottery to discuss how new homes should be built. The members met on several weekends, listened to experts, and talked with local people. At the end, they wrote a report with recommendations for the town council. The council has promised to read the report carefully before it makes a final decision. Supporters say that this kind of assembly gives ordinary people a real voice in politics, and that it helps residents trust the decisions that are made.
translation: ヨーロッパのある小さな町で、普通の住民40人が抽選で選ばれ、新しい住宅をどう建てるべきかを話し合うことになった。メンバーは週末に数回集まり、専門家の話を聞き、地元の人々と話をした。最後に彼らは、町議会への提言をまとめた報告書を書いた。議会は、最終的な決定をする前に報告書を注意深く読むと約束している。支持者は、この種の会議が普通の人々に政治で本当の発言力を与え、決められた事柄を住民が信頼する助けになると言う。

questions.question: How were the members of the assembly selected?
choices: By random selection among local residents
Through a national election
By applying for seats on the council
By choosing volunteers from political parties
questions.explanation: 「chosen by lottery」より、住民の中から無作為の抽選で選ばれた。選挙、応募、政党からの選出は本文にない。

questions.question: What will the town council do with the report?
choices: Build the new homes immediately
Ask the national government to cancel the plan
Hire the members as full-time staff
Read it carefully before making a decision
questions.explanation: 「read the report carefully before it makes a final decision」より、決定の前に報告書を注意深く読む。すぐに建設する、計画を取り消す、委員を職員として雇う、は本文にない。

title: Recess and concentration
script: Narrator: Many primary schools have cut their daily break time to make room for more lessons. However, a number of teachers have noticed that children become restless and find it harder to concentrate in the afternoon. In one school, the head teacher decided to bring back a fifteen-minute recess after lunch. Within a few weeks, teachers reported that the children were calmer and more focused in class. The head teacher believes that a short break is not wasted time, but a part of learning.
translation: 多くの小学校が、授業時間を増やすために毎日の休み時間を減らしてきた。しかし、子どもたちが落ち着きをなくし、午後は集中しにくくなると気づいた教師も少なくない。ある学校では、校長先生が昼食後に15分の休み時間を再び設けることを決めた。数週間のうちに、教師たちは子どもたちが以前より落ち着き、授業に集中するようになったと報告した。校長先生は、短い休み時間は無駄な時間ではなく、学びの一部だと考えている。

questions.question: What did teachers notice after the recess was brought back?
choices: Students finished their homework faster.
Students asked for longer school days.
Teachers stopped giving any homework.
Children were calmer and more focused.
questions.explanation: 「the children were calmer and more focused」より、休み時間の復活後に子どもたちが落ち着いて集中するようになった。宿題が早く終わる、授業時間を延ばす、宿題をなくす、は本文にない。

questions.question: Who decided to bring back the recess?
choices: The parents of the students
The local government
The head teacher of the school
The school board
questions.explanation: 「the head teacher decided to bring back a fifteen-minute recess」より、休み時間を復活させたのは校長先生。保護者、地方自治体、教育委員会の決定は本文にない。

title: Rent control debate
script: Narrator: In many large cities, rents have risen faster than wages, and many young families now spend most of their income on housing. To protect tenants, some local governments have introduced rent control, which limits how much landlords can raise the rent each year. Supporters argue that it keeps people in their homes and prevents sudden evictions. Critics, however, say that rent control discourages landlords from maintaining buildings and reduces the number of new apartments being built. Many economists therefore suggest a middle path: building more affordable housing while still protecting long-term tenants. Local officials admit that the debate is far from settled.
translation: 多くの大都市では、家賃が賃金より速く上がり、若い家族の多くが今では収入の大半を住居費に充てている。借家人を守るため、一部の自治体は家賃規制を導入した。これは、大家が毎年家賃を上げられる額を制限する制度である。支持者は、この制度によって人々が住み続けられ、突然の立ち退きを防げると主張する。しかし批判する人々は、家賃規制によって大家が建物の維持に消極的になり、新しく建てられるアパートの数も減ると言う。そのため多くの経済学者は、手頃な住宅を増やしつつ、長く住んでいる借家人を守り続けるという中間の道を提案している。地方自治体の職員も、議論はまだ決着していないと認めている。

questions.question: What is the main purpose of rent control?
choices: To encourage landlords to build more apartments
To protect renters from sudden increases
To lower the cost of constructing new buildings
To reduce the number of families in large cities
questions.explanation: 家賃の値上げを制限して、借家人を守る制度だと説明されている。大家に建設を促す、建設費を下げる、大都市の家族を減らす、は本文にない。

questions.question: What do many economists suggest?
choices: Ending all limits on rent increases in cities
Encouraging families to move to rural towns
Building affordable housing while protecting long-term tenants
Banning the construction of new apartments
questions.explanation: 「a middle path」として、手頃な住宅を建てつつ長期の借家人を守ることを提案している。家賃規制の全廃、地方への移住、新しいアパートの建設禁止は本文にない。

title: Hiring for skills, not degrees
script: Narrator: For decades, many employers asked for a university degree before they would even interview a candidate. Now a growing number of companies are dropping that requirement for many jobs. They focus instead on skills that can be tested, such as writing a sample report or solving a practical problem during an interview. Human resources managers say that this approach helps them find talented people who would otherwise have been overlooked. It also allows workers who learned their skills through training programs or on the job to move into better positions. Some experts warn, however, that companies need to design their tests carefully, so that they really measure what the job requires.
translation: 何十年ものあいだ、多くの雇用主は、候補者と面接する前に大学の学位を求めてきた。今では、多くの職種でその条件をなくす企業が増えている。その代わりに、テストできる能力、たとえば見本のレポートを書くことや、面接中に実務的な問題を解くことに注目している。人事担当者は、このやり方によって、それまでなら見過ごされていた有能な人材を見つけられると言う。また、研修や職場で技能を身につけた人が、より良いポストに就けるようにもなる。しかし一部の専門家は、企業がテストを慎重に設計し、仕事に本当に必要なことを測れるようにする必要があると警告している。

questions.question: What do some companies now do instead of requiring degrees?
choices: They hire only graduates from famous universities
They evaluate what applicants can actually do
They offer degrees to their own employees
They stop interviewing candidates altogether
questions.explanation: 学位の代わりに、応募者が実際にできることを評価すると説明されている。名門大学の卒業生に限る、社員に学位を与える、面接をやめる、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why do the managers think the new approach is helpful?
choices: It saves money on job advertisements.
It makes interviews much shorter.
It reveals talented people they might have missed.
It lets applicants avoid taking any tests.
questions.explanation: 人事担当者は、従来なら見落とされた優秀な人を見つけられると話している。広告費、面接時間、テストの免除は本文にない。

title: Traffic cameras and public trust
script: Narrator: A city council recently installed speed cameras along several busy roads. Officials said the cameras were meant to protect children on their way to school, and they expected accidents to fall. Within a year, however, many drivers complained that the cameras were placed in spots where the limit seemed unnecessarily low. Some residents began to suspect that the goal was to raise money from fines rather than to make the streets safer. The council has since published a map of all camera locations and the reasons for each one, which residents can now check on the council's website. A spokesperson said that this openness was necessary, because a rule is only respected when people believe it was made fairly.
translation: ある市議会は最近、交通量の多いいくつかの道路に速度違反を取り締まるカメラを設置した。当局は、カメラは通学途中の子どもを守るためのもので、事故が減ると期待していると述べた。しかし1年のうちに、制限速度が必要以上に低く感じられる場所にカメラがあると、多くのドライバーが不満を訴えた。一部の住民は、道路を安全にするよりも、罰金で収入を得ることが目的ではないかと疑い始めた。その後、市議会はすべてのカメラの位置と設置理由を示す地図を公開し、住民が市議会のウェブサイトで確認できるようにした。広報担当者は、この情報公開は必要だったと述べた。規則は、人々がそれを公正に作られたと信じて初めて守られるからだ。

questions.question: What did drivers complain about?
choices: The cameras were placed too far from the schools.
The fines were too small to change behavior.
The limits were set unfairly low in certain areas.
The map of the camera locations was never published.
questions.explanation: ドライバーは、制限速度が不必要に低く設定されていると不満を述べた。学校からの距離、罰金の額は不満として本文にない。地図は後に公開されている。

questions.question: Why does the spokesperson say that openness is necessary?
choices: Drivers always break rules unless they are fined.
Transparency helps people accept rules they believe are fair.
Fines are the only reliable way to improve safety.
The council should remove all cameras from the roads.
questions.explanation: 「a rule is only respected when people believe it was made fairly」より、公正だと信じられてこそ規則が守られるので、情報公開が必要だという理屈。ドライバーは罰金がないと規則を破る、罰金だけが方法、カメラを撤去すべき、は本文にない。

title: Hand hygiene in hospitals
script: Narrator: Doctors and nurses are taught that washing hands is the simplest way to prevent infections in hospitals, yet surveys show that the rule is often ignored during busy shifts. One hospital in a large city decided to try a different approach. Instead of relying on posters, it placed small sensors near the entrance to each ward, and the sensors recorded every time hand sanitizer was used. Each month, nurses were shown their own results. At first, some staff felt they were being watched, but over time most agreed that the information helped them keep a routine that is easy to neglect under pressure. The number of infections in the hospital dropped noticeably in the following year.
translation: 医師や看護師は、手を洗うことが病院での感染を防ぐ最も簡単な方法だと教えられている。それでも、忙しい勤務中にはこのルールが守られないことが多いという調査結果がある。大都市のある病院は、別のやり方を試すことにした。ポスターに頼る代わりに、各病棟の入口の近くに小型のセンサーを置き、消毒液が使われるたびに記録した。毎月、看護師たちは自分の結果を見せられた。当初は見張られていると感じるスタッフもいたが、時間がたつと、ほとんどの人が、その情報のおかげで、プレッシャーがかかると忘れやすい習慣を続けられたと認めた。病院の感染者数は、翌年に目立って減少した。

questions.question: How did the hospital monitor hand cleaning?
choices: By asking nurses to fill in weekly paper forms
By using devices that tracked sanitizer usage
By hiring extra staff to wash hands for others
By putting up new posters in every room
questions.explanation: 消毒液の使用を記録するセンサーを使った。ポスターは使わなかったと述べられている。週ごとの紙の記録、代わりに手を洗う人員の配置は本文にない。

questions.question: Why did the nurses find the monthly results helpful?
choices: The data showed that the sensors were working perfectly.
The data proved that other hospitals had failed.
The data reminded them of a habit they tended to neglect when busy.
The data let them compare their salaries with other staff.
questions.explanation: 「a routine that is easy to neglect under pressure」が根拠。忙しいときに忘れがちな習慣を思い出させたのが、結果の情報だと説明されている。センサーの完全な動作、他病院の失敗、給与の比較は本文にない。

title: Universal basic income pilot
script: Narrator: A pilot program in a rural region gave a fixed monthly payment to every adult, with no conditions attached. Early reports suggested that people did not stop working, as many critics had predicted. Instead, some participants used the money to return to school, and others started small businesses. Most residents of the region were generally satisfied, and many said the money reduced their anxiety about everyday bills. However, the researchers also noted that the payments were not large enough to cover housing costs in the cities, and families living there reported little change. The program's designers have therefore recommended testing the idea in urban areas before any national policy is considered. They argue that the results so far are encouraging, though far from conclusive.
translation: ある農村地域で試験的に行われた制度では、すべての成人に、条件をつけずに毎月一定額が支給された。初期の報告では、批判する人々が予想したように、人々が働くのをやめることはなかったとされている。その代わりに、学校に戻るために資金を使った参加者もいれば、小さな事業を始めた人もいた。地域の住民の多くは概ね満足しており、毎日の支払いへの不安が減ったと話す人も多かった。しかし研究者はまた、支給額は都市の住居費をまかなうには十分でなく、都市部の家族には大きな変化が見られなかったとも指摘した。そのため制度を設計した人々は、国の政策を検討する前に都市部でも試すことを勧めている。彼らは、これまでの結果は励みになるが、決定的ではないと主張する。

questions.question: Why do the program's designers recommend testing the idea in cities?
choices: The payment did not meet the high living costs in urban areas.
Participants in the rural region had all stopped working.
Critics had proven that people always quit their jobs.
The national government had already approved the policy.
questions.explanation: 「not large enough to cover housing costs in the cities」より、都市の住居費に対して支給額が足りず、農村の結果が都市にも当てはまるか分からないため。働くのをやめた、批判者が証明した、政府がすでに承認した、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker imply about the results so far?
choices: They show that the policy should be introduced nationwide.
They are promising but do not yet prove the idea works.
They confirm that people stopped working once they received the payment.
They prove that rural families spend most of their money on housing.
questions.explanation: 「encouraging, though far from conclusive」より、結果は有望だが決定的ではないと考えている。全国導入、支給後の離職、農村の家族の住居費への支出は本文と合わない。

title: Public bathhouses
script: Narrator: For generations, public bathhouses were the center of neighborhood life in many Japanese towns. People came not only to wash, but also to chat, exchange news, and watch over the children of their neighbors. Today, however, the number of these bathhouses has fallen sharply, mainly because more homes now have private bathrooms. Some owners have tried to keep their businesses alive by adding hot springs, cafes, or relaxation rooms. Yet the most successful ones seem to be those that have kept their original role as a meeting place for the local community. A few young people have recently begun visiting old bathhouses, and they say that they feel calm there in a way they cannot in modern spas. Regular customers often describe the warm, quiet atmosphere as something rarely found in busy city life.
translation: 何世代にもわたって、公衆浴場は多くの日本の町で近所の人々の暮らしの中心だった。人々は体を洗うためだけでなく、おしゃべりをしたり、ニュースを交換したり、近所の子どもを見守ったりするために訪れた。しかし今では、家庭に個人用の浴室が増えたことを主な理由として、こうした浴場の数は急に減っている。経営者の中には、温泉や喫茶室、くつろぎの部屋を加えて商売を続けようとした人もいる。それでも、もっとも成功しているのは、地域の人が集まる場所という本来の役割を保ってきた店のようだ。最近は古い銭湯を訪れる若い人も出てきており、彼らは現代の温泉施設にはない落ち着きをそこで感じると話す。常連客は、この温かく静かな雰囲気は、忙しい都会の暮らしではめったに得られないものだと言う。

questions.question: Why are some bathhouses still able to attract visitors?
choices: They still serve as meeting places for local residents.
They have become cheaper than private bathrooms in new homes.
They have banned children from visiting the premises.
They offer more hot springs than any other spa in Japan.
questions.explanation: 「kept their original role as a meeting place」より、地域の人が集まる場としての役割を保った施設が成功していると説明されている。安さ、子どもの入場禁止、温泉の多さは本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about young visitors?
choices: They are attracted to a sense of peace that modern spas lack.
They are mainly interested in the low prices of old bathhouses.
They want to replace bathhouses with private bathrooms.
They hope to find jobs in the bathhouse business.
questions.explanation: 若い人は古い銭湯で、現代の温泉施設にはない落ち着きを感じると話している。安さへの関心、家庭の浴室への置き換え、就職の話は本文にない。

title: A downtown car ban that changed twice
script: Narrator: The city first announced that it would ban private cars from the downtown area on weekdays, in order to reduce traffic and pollution. Shop owners protested that customers would stop coming, so the plan was changed to a weekend-only ban. Then a traffic study showed that most of the congestion was caused by delivery trucks, not by private cars, and officials dropped the weekend plan entirely. Instead, they will restrict delivery trucks to early morning hours and set aside special loading zones along the main streets. Several residents had argued that a car ban would hurt the elderly and people with disabilities, and officials agreed that exemptions would be needed for them. The new arrangement will be reviewed after six months, and the city has promised to publish the results for everyone to see. Business groups have welcomed the change, although some of them still worry about the cost of new signs.
translation: 市は当初、交通量と排気ガスを減らすため、平日に中心部への自家用車の乗り入れを禁止すると発表した。店主たちは、客が来なくなると反対したため、計画は週末だけの禁止に変更された。その後の交通調査で、渋滞の大半は自家用車ではなく配送トラックが原因だと分かり、当局は週末の計画を完全に取りやめた。代わりに、配送トラックの走行を早朝に限り、主要な通りに専用の荷下ろし区域を設ける。数人の住民が、車の禁止は高齢者や障害のある人を苦しめると主張し、当局も、そうした人々には例外が必要だと認めた。新しい方式は6か月後に見直され、市は結果を誰でも見られるように公表すると約束している。商工団体はこの変更を歓迎しているが、新しい標識の費用を心配する団体もある。

questions.question: What is the city's current plan for downtown traffic?
choices: Ban private cars from downtown on weekdays.
Allow cars downtown only on weekends.
Keep the downtown area open to all traffic without changes.
Limit trucks to early hours and designate areas for unloading.
questions.explanation: 最終的に決まったのは、配送トラックを早朝に限り、荷下ろし用の区域を設けることだ。平日の車両禁止と週末だけの禁止は、いずれも途中で取り下げられた案。全面的な変更なしは本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why did officials drop the weekend-only plan?
choices: A study found that trucks, not cars, were responsible for the congestion.
Shop owners asked for a full ban on delivery trucks.
Residents asked for a full ban on cars all week long.
The city lacked the funds needed to install new signs.
questions.explanation: 交通調査で、渋滞の主な原因は自家用車ではなく配送トラックだと分かり、週末だけの案が取り下げられた。店主の要求、住民が全日の車両禁止を求めた、財源不足は本文にない。

title: A battery claim that was withdrawn
script: Narrator: In an early announcement, a research team said its new battery material would allow electric cars to be charged in just a few minutes. The claim attracted enormous attention, and several companies announced plans based on it. Investors poured money into related firms, and their share prices rose sharply for a few weeks. However, when independent laboratories tried to repeat the experiment, they could not get the same results. The team later admitted that a measurement error had made the original data look far better than it really was. It withdrew its claim and said that the material might still be useful, but only for small devices such as sensors. Several of the companies that had made plans have since quietly stopped talking about them. Its next report will focus on whether the material can be made cheaply enough for mass production.
translation: 初期の発表で、ある研究チームは、新しい電池材料によって電気自動車が数分で充電できるようになると発表した。この主張は大きな注目を集め、いくつかの企業はそれをもとにした計画を発表した。投資家は関連企業に多額の資金を注ぎ、株価は数週間のあいだ大きく上がった。しかし、独立した研究所が同じ実験を繰り返そうとしたところ、同じ結果は得られなかった。その後チームは、測定の誤りによって元のデータが実際よりずっと良く見えていたことを認めた。チームは主張を取り下げ、この材料はセンサーのような小型の機器に限れば役立つかもしれないと述べた。計画を立てていた企業のいくつかは、その後その話題に静かに触れなくなった。次の報告では、この材料を大量生産できるほど安く作れるかどうかに焦点を当てるという。

questions.question: What is the team's current view of its battery material?
choices: It can charge electric cars in just a few minutes.
It is ready for mass production in cars.
Independent laboratories have confirmed its performance.
It could be practical only for tiny gadgets, not vehicles.
questions.explanation: 「useful, but only for small devices such as sensors」より、小型の機器に限って役立つ可能性がある。急速充電の主張は撤回され、車への量産は本文で見通せていない。独立機関による確認はなかった。

questions.question: Why did the team withdraw its original claim?
choices: Investors demanded that the team stop its research.
The government banned all research on battery materials.
Companies complained that the plan was too expensive.
A mistake in its measurements had made the data look more promising.
questions.explanation: 測定の誤りによって元のデータが実際より良く見えていたと、チームが認めたことが理由。投資家の要求、政府の禁止、企業の不満は本文にない。
